settings.title: Two Rustic Looms & A Defiant Dream
settings.body_text: In 1986, in an arid courtyard in rural Rajasthan, our founder observed a profound injustice: ancient Indian carpet weaving was being exploited by predatory intermediaries. He borrowed a small sum, built two vertical timber looms, and made an unprecedented pact: to work directly with rural families at their doorstep.

settings.title: The Manchaha Movement: Artisans as Fine Artists
settings.body_text: In 2012, we introduced Manchaha ('from the heart')—giving rural weavers leftover yarn and absolute artistic freedom to design rugs without presets. They wove village monsoons, starry desert skies, and ancestral stories. The tapestries stunned international collectors at Milan Design Week.

settings.heading: Every Knot a Heartbeat, Every Rug a Genealogic Tapestry
settings.subtext: We believe true luxury is slow, conscious, and human. In an age of ephemeral mass production, an Indian Rug Store creation stands as an enduring heirloom—hand-tied by rural artisans who weave memory, devotion, and landscape into every square inch.
